newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 75 cts up, Brent flat to 5 cts dn.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 75 cts up, Brent flat to 5 cts dn.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open 50 cents to $1 a tonne firmer on Thursday but Brent could slip back early, dealers said.
July gas oil settled at $167.50 a tonne on Wednesday, missing out on much of Brent's modest rally into the close prompted by short-covering and a tight cash market.
Dealers said positive chart signals could help push gas oil even higher in early dealing but deteriorating fundamentals would act as a brake.
"Technically gas oil is looking good but there are still good offers on the physical market," said a broker.
August gas oil settled at $169 a tonne, a previous resistance level which should now provide support, he added.
August Brent was trading at $18.90 a barrel by 0754 GMT in Singapore, two cents down on its London settlement, a move expected to be reflected in early IPE dealing.

But a tight cash Brent market -- one major oil company is sitting on over half of the July programme released so far -- was boosting intermonth spreads and keeping prompt values buoyant, brokers said.
"Nearly all the volume yesterday came in the Brent spreads and gas oil was just moving up on the back of that," said one.

Despite Brent's strength, some brokers saw little fundamental reason for the complex generally to move higher given rising U.S. distillate stocks and a growing consensus that Iraq will resume exports in early August.
Much of Wednesday's 12-cent gains were attributed to funds covering short positions ahead of the long holiday weekend.
IPE crude trading will close early on Thursday, at 1630 GMT (1730 local time) to allow for Independence Day holidays in the U.S. NYMEX will close early on Thursday and reopen on Monday July 7.
